about: Skills tool: rates of change and percent change. Solver and generator: ApBioProblems, kind rates (mode rate or pct). early and late are pairs of INDEXES into times (the two readings a rate is taken between).
intro: Work out how fast something changes from a table of measurements, and compare samples fairly with percent change.
howItWorksTitle: The formulas, and how answers are checked
howItWorks:
rate = Δy / Δt = (y₂ − y₁) / (t₂ − t₁)

percent change = (final − initial) / initial × 100

  • A rate always has a unit made of two units: the amount per unit of time (for example mL/min).
  • Percent change compares each sample with its own starting value. A loss gives a negative percent change: keep the sign.
  • An answer counts when it is within one unit of the last decimal place asked for, or within 1%.

explore.refHtml:
The formulas

rate = Δy / Δt = (y₂ − y₁) / (t₂ − t₁)

The AP® Biology formula sheet writes a rate as dY/dt: dY is the amount of change and dt is the change in time. From a data table, take the change between two readings and divide by the time between them. The unit is always the amount per unit of time (here mL/min).

percent change = (final − initial) / initial × 100

Divide by the initial (start) value, and keep the sign: a loss is negative.

Average rate and rate at a moment

The slope between two readings is the average rate over that interval. The rate at one moment is the slope of the tangent, a line that just touches the curve there: pick any run along it, read the rise, and divide. Here the curve is a smooth line through the six readings, so a tangent's slope is an estimate.

Why this run slows down

Catalase breaks hydrogen peroxide into water and oxygen. As the hydrogen peroxide is used up, fewer substrate molecules meet an active site each second, so less oxygen is made each minute: the curve flattens and the rate falls.
